chapter.title: What Are Design Patterns? Why Use Them?

payload.markdown: No matter how elegant the solution (and some are very elegant indeed), the problem and its context are the grounds of a pattern. Recognizing a problem is harder than applying any one of the solutions in a pattern catalog. This is one reason that some pattern solutions can be misapplied or overused.

blocks.text: No matter how elegant the solution (and some are very elegant indeed), the problem and its context are the grounds of a pattern. Recognizing a problem is harder than applying any one of the solutions in a pattern catalog. This is one reason that some pattern solutions can be misapplied or overused.

payload.markdown: Patterns describe a problem space with great care. The problem is described in brief and then contextualized, often with a typical example and one or more diagrams. It is broken down into its specifics, its various manifestations. Any warning signs that might help in identifying the problem are described.

items: Behavioral Patterns: Patterns that distribute responsibility and coordinate behaviour.
Creational Patterns: Patterns that control how objects come into being.
Enterprise Patterns: Patterns for service layers, domain objects and application architecture.
Error Patterns: Repeatable strategies: fail fast, wrap and rethrow, aggregate and report.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
Pattern Principles: What design patterns are, how to describe them, and when one fits.
Persistence Patterns: Patterns that map objects to storage: data mapper, identity map, unit of work.
Strategy Pattern: Swapping an algorithm behind a common interface at runtime.
